extracted.intended_audience: researchers, instructors, and graduate students working in undergraduate mathematics education; RUME conference participants and paper authors
extracted.subtask_description: Conference proceedings (RUME Volume 3) containing contributed and preliminary research reports on undergraduate mathematics education, including empirical studies, instructional design reports, and discourse analyses. The document both reports individual study methods/results and states conference review/acceptance practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review requirement for Volumes 1 and 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference papers included in Volumes 1 and 2 underwent a rigorous review by two or more reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These papers represent current important work in the field and are elaborations of the RUME conference reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best paper award criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Winner of the best paper award is an honor bestowed upon papers that make a substantial contribution to the field in terms of raising new questions or gaining insights into existing research programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to distinguish exceptionally impactful papers in the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributed Research Reports acceptance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributed Research Reports were presented at the conference and underwent a rigorous review by at least three reviewers prior to the conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reports discuss completed research studies on undergraduate mathematics education and address findings, contemporary theoretical perspectives, and research paradigms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Research Reports acceptance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary Research Reports were presented at the conference and underwent a rigorous review by at least three reviewers prior to the conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary Reports discuss ongoing and exploratory research studies; significant discussion time followed each presentation to allow for feedback and suggestions for future research directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Halliday's three functional components for discourse analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze textbook language using Halliday's (1978) functional components: ideational, interpersonal, and textual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ideational component addresses the view of mathematics presented; the interpersonal component examines social/personal roles (e.g., pronoun use, imperatives, modality); the textual component describes exposition mode, themes, and argument forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpersonal linguistic markers for textbook voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure first- and second-person pronouns, imperatives, and modal verbs as indicators of the author's relationship to the reader and inclusivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts/frequencies of 'we/us/our', 'you', imperatives (consider, find, determine), and modality (may, can, possibly) indicate degree of inclusion, invitation to reflect, or assertion of certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textual linguistic markers for dialogic style
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess textual features such as mode of discourse (exposition), use of questions, and narrative forms to determine conversational or dialogic style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low question frequency indicates a less dialogic, more expository textbook voice; mode of exposition shows how mathematics content is organized and presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideational markers and view of mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate content/meaning and authorial stance to infer whether the textbook portrays mathematics as fixed/absolute/formal or inclusive/access-oriented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare similarity of content across texts and linguistic encodings that reveal the author's vision of mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook analysis sampling method
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample the 10–14 pages from each textbook covering the exposition of the concept (here: function) including introductory commentary and definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mine sampled pages for linguistic markers corresponding to the three functional components; this sampling is presented as an objective means to study the 'voice' of textbooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational definition of student success
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'success' as an indicator variable coded 1 if a student obtains a passing grade and 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This combines effects of pass rate and dropout rate and serves as a primary dependent variable when evaluating pedagogical interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational definition of dropout
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'dropout' as an indicator variable coded 1 if a student dropped out of a course and 0 if a student completed the course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a dependent variable to analyze retention separately from course passing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key independent variables for instructional-effect studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Include student gender, race/ethnicity (White, Black, Hispanic, Other), prior mathematics knowledge (ACT math score), course repeat status ('redo'), and instructional method (e.g., MMM vs conventional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These covariates control for student background and allow assessment of differential impacts across subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimation approach and reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Fit regression models (including interactive models) to estimate effects of instructional methods on success and dropout; report odds ratios, interaction effects, sample sizes, and statistical significance (p-values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both descriptive statistics and regression outputs; include significance thresholds (e.g., p<0.01, p<0.05, p<0.1) and interpret magnitudes (e.g., percent change in odds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness metrics for pedagogical interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate interventions using pass rates, withdrawal/dropout rates, changes in odds of success, and measures of achievement-gap reduction between demographic groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present both absolute percentages (e.g., percent passing) and model-adjusted effect sizes (odds ratios, interaction multipliers) to capture practical and statistical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description/specification of blended learning intervention (MMM)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Memphis Mathematics Method substitutes brief lectures with lab sessions using MyMathLab; students spend ~30 class hours practicing problems on MyMathLab over a 15-week semester; the system is used for instruction, course management, and grading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear specification of the pedagogy is required to interpret outcomes and replicate the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergent models heuristic (instructional-design rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the four-layer emergent-model heuristic (Situational, Referential, General, Formal) from Realistic Mathematics Education to design instruction and to trace student reasoning evolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should begin with experientially real tasks (situational), enable students to generate models that reference the task (referential), develop general models for broader interpretation (general), and culminate in formal mathematical reasoning (formal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional design criteria: task progression and intellectual need
rubrics_metrics.description: Design sequences that create an intellectual need for formal strategies by starting from intuitive/experiential contexts and progressing to abstraction (e.g., Magic Carpet tasks leading to definitions of span and linear independence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tasks should be experientially real, scaffold transitions from model-of to model-for, and intentionally delay formal methods until students see the need for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection standards for classroom teaching experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect video recordings of classroom episodes, produce transcriptions, gather daily reflections and homework, and document iteration across terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These multiple data sources support rich qualitative analysis of student reasoning and the tracing of emergent models over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task-level design and pacing guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate roughly one class day per task in an instructional sequence that moves students from situational engagement to formalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a series of scaffolded tasks (e.g., four or five tasks such as the Magic Carpet Ride sequence) to guide students through situational → referential → general → formal activity.
